_doc: GENERATED by tools/read_stated_kinship.py --build; gated by --check, which re-derives the counts and holds every row here against the committed household records. The landed rows and the refusals are hand-authored in this file and adjudicated one by one; the COUNTS are derived, so a pair nobody has ruled on cannot hide.
what: Every kinship the committed corpus STATES between two people, held against data/residents/. A relationship already carried inside one household by persons[].relationship is not in scope: this pass is about the ties that cross two records, which before it had nowhere to go but prose.
the_rule: A row lands only when the source states the relationship in its own words AND both ends are people this layer already holds. The identity of each end is either exact (the source names them) or carried by a stated rule, and which it is is written into the row's confidence: attested where the page names both, inferred where a binding was read. NO RELATIONSHIP IS INFERRED FROM A SHARED SURNAME. A refusal is declared as explicitly as a landing.
the_finding: Before this pass 2 kin rows existed (the Kinzie half brothers, T-0597) and 24 people carried a relationship inside a household, out of 1,362. The corpus states 16 further ties. Five land as 10 reciprocal rows and eleven are refused, and the refusals are the more useful half: ONLY ONE of them fails for want of evidence about the relationship. The rest fail because the OTHER PERSON IS NOT IN THIS LAYER — a bride at Naperville, a Potawatomi chief at the Calumet, an unnamed daughter of Payne, and above all the 54 married couples of St Mary's baptismal register, 85 of whose Chicago adults reach no surname here at all. The town is thin on kinship mainly because it is thin on women and on the French, Metis, Irish and German Catholic households the poll books never recorded, and the ties will arrive when those people do, not before.

landed.statement: Andreas's life of Dr Elijah Dewey Harmon lists his five surviving children: 'Charles Loomis Harmon, Isaac Dewey Harmon, Harriet Harmon, Lucretia Harmon, and Welthyan Loomis Harmon.'
landed.identity: Both ends are named in the quoted list under their full names and the doctor is the man whose life it is. No identity rule is needed.

landed.statement: The same sentence: 'Charles Loomis Harmon, Isaac Dewey Harmon, Harriet Harmon, Lucretia Harmon, and Welthyan Loomis Harmon.'
landed.identity: Both ends are named in the quoted list under their full names. No identity rule is needed.

landed.statement: hh_beaubien_mark's arrival note, citing Andreas: 'Andreas's life of his brother Jean Baptiste gives the family's trading history at Milwaukee from about 1800 and the move to Chicago in 1812; Mark's own route is not traced.'
landed.identity: Both cards are individually unambiguous — one Mark Beaubien, one Col. Jean Baptiste Beaubien. INFERRED because no page of Andreas is quoted verbatim for the relationship: what the corpus holds is this project's summary of the passage.

landed.statement: hh_beaubien_madore: 'He is the son of Jean Baptiste Beaubien by his first wife Mah-naw-bun-no-quah, an Ottawa woman'; hh_beaubien_jean_baptiste, from the other side: he 'married first Mah-naw-bun-no-quah, an Ottawa woman, the mother of his sons Charles Henry and Madore'.
landed.identity: Both cards are individually unambiguous. INFERRED on the same ground as the brother row: the corpus holds this project's reading of Andreas rather than a quoted page.

landed.statement: Andreas, verbatim, in the clause that gives John his trade: 'John Miller, brother of Samuel, the landlord, came in 1831, and run a tannery just north of Miller's tavern.'
landed.identity: THE INFERENCE IS THE IDENTITY, NOT THE KINSHIP. Andreas writes 'Samuel, the landlord'. This layer holds one Samuel Miller (hh_miller_samuel, civic pass, 1832 muster + 1833 tax list + Chicago Democrat), forename and surname agreeing exactly, and hh_miller_john's own lives_at note already reads miller_house as 'Samuel's house, not John's'. The binding is a reading, so the row is inferred.

refusals.statement: Andreas's 1833 roster, quoted on hh_clybourne_archibald: 'Julia K. Clark, half-brother of A. Clybourne, then living with him'.
refusals.reason: THE RELATIONSHIP IS STATED AND THE IDENTITY IS NOT. The forename as printed is 'Julia' against the word 'half-brother', so the reading is already known to be damaged; binding it to hh_clark_john_k ('John K Clark', a civic-mint card off the poll and tax lists) is an OCR correction and an identity ruling, which is a different pass from this one. The Clybourne card also says Clark is 'written into this household' and he is not — the card carries one person. Filed as its own ticket.

refusals.statement: hh_kinzie_james carries, in prose and citing nothing, that James is half brother to Robert A. Kinzie as well as to John H.
refusals.reason: ALREADY SOMEBODY ELSE'S TICKET, AND THE FAR END IS NOT SETTLED. T-0732 is open on exactly this claim and on the two Robert Kinzie households it would have to choose between. A kin row written here would pre-empt that ruling.

refusals.statement: hh_taylor_augustine's research_note: 'one of two Taylor brothers in this parcel - Anson H. Taylor hauled the lumber for the same church with his own team and has his own household.'
refusals.reason: NO SOURCE STATES IT. The phrase is this project's own, and read strictly it says there are two Taylors doing carpentry work on the same church, not that they are brothers. Anson H. Taylor's documented brother is Charles H. Taylor, who is already a person inside hh_taylor_anson. Nine Taylors are carried here; a tie on the surname is the exact move T-0734's acceptance forbids.

refusals.statement: hh_beaubien_jean_baptiste: he 'married first Mah-naw-bun-no-quah, an Ottawa woman, the mother of his sons Charles Henry and Madore'.
refusals.reason: THE BROTHERHOOD IS STATED; THE CARD IS NOT RULED. hh_beaubien_charles_h is one of the unruled Beaubien cards in the cluster T-0839 is adjudicating, alongside hh_beaubien_b, hh_beaubien_medard, hh_beaubien_medore_b, hh_beaubien_john_s and hh_beaubien_alexandre. Binding a relationship to a card whose identity is unruled would launder that ruling. The father tie to Madore, whose card is not in doubt, IS landed.

refusals.statement: hh_robinson_alexander: Catherine Chevalier is 'daughter of Francois and Mary Ann Chevalier, her father chief of a united band of Potawatomi, Ottawa and Chippewa with his village at the Calumet'.
refusals.reason: THE FAR END IS NOT A PERSON THIS LAYER HOLDS. Neither Francois nor Mary Ann Chevalier has a record, and a kin row links two committed records. Minting them is a resident pass, not this one. Alexander Robinson's own tie to Catherine is already carried inside the household as persons[].relationship 'wife'.

refusals.statement: hh_pruyne_kimberly, from Andreas's footnote: 'on August 20, 1835 Peter Pruyne married Rebecca, only daughter of Silas W.' — and separately that Pruyne 'is married at Chicago on 20 August 1835, seven weeks after the scene date'.
refusals.reason: THE FAR END IS NOT A PERSON THIS LAYER HOLDS, AND THE MARRIAGE IS AFTER THE SCENE DATE. Neither the bride nor her father has a record; the wedding falls seven weeks past 1835-07-01, so it is not a relationship in the modelled year at all.

refusals.statement: hh_hobson_jesse: 'Jesse Hobson was living in Cook County in 1835 and married Catherine Daugherty at Naperville on April 6, 1835.'
refusals.reason: THE FAR END IS NOT A PERSON THIS LAYER HOLDS. Catherine Daugherty has no record and the marriage is at Naperville, outside the modelled town.

refusals.statement: hh_paddock_jane: 'Cook County history says Samuel Mahaffay, a Palos settler of 1834, married Jane Paddock in 1835.'
refusals.reason: THE FAR END IS NOT A PERSON THIS LAYER HOLDS. Samuel Mahaffay is a Palos settler with no record here.

refusals.statement: hh_trimble_edward: Kane County history 'notes his marriage to a daughter of Payne'.
refusals.reason: THE FAR END IS NOT NAMED. 'A daughter of Payne' is not a person, and this project does not mint one to hang a relationship on.

refusals.statement: St Mary's baptismal register, 1833-1835: 54 of its entries name a father and a mother together, which is a documented couple in each case.
refusals.reason: FOUR OF THE 54 TOUCH A PERSON THIS LAYER HOLDS, AND IN EVERY ONE OF THE FOUR THE OTHER PARENT DOES NOT EXIST HERE — Mark Beaubien with Monique Nadeau (1833 entries 1 and 19), Solomon Juneau with Josette Vieau (1833 entry 5), Mary Durbin with Samuel Hendriks (1834 entry 8). The register is the largest untapped seam of stated kinship in the corpus and it is untappable until its people are minted; the crosswalk's own rule says so ('Nothing here mints or regrades a resident'), and 85 of its Chicago adults reach no surname in this layer at all.

refusals.statement: Six households carry a family the source COUNTS but never names — Heacock's 'a wife and five sons by the spring of 1835', Elijah Garton's 'his wife and six children', Owen's family, the four Temple children, and the two unnamed Beaubien and Robinson households.
refusals.reason: A COUNT IS NOT A NAME. Each is already carried as far as the evidence allows: an aggregate person inside the household with relationship 'household_member' or 'child'. A kin row needs two named people at two records and there is only one name in each of these.
